question.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal.
question.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1}\},$ $\text{Span}\{{a}_{2}\},$ and $\text{Span}\{{a}_{3}\}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{0\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 1+0\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=0[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{0\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot 1+0\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=0[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{(0)(0)+(-1)(-1)+(0)(2)+(1)(-1)}{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}{a}_{2}=0[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Note:** Since we got the zero-vector as the projection, the vector $x$ must be  orthogonal to the subspace $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}\}.$ Thus, the vector $x$ extends the given set to an orthogonal basis of ${R}^{4}.$
